question: Let $f(x)=\min(e^x,e^{-x})$ for any real number $x$. Then

options.B: $f$ attains its maximum at a point where $f\prime(x)=0$;
options.C: $f$ attains its maximum at a point where it is not differentiable;
options.D: $M:=\max\{f(x):x\text{ real}\}<\infty$ but there is no number $x_0$ such that $f(x_0)=M$.
